currentCondition: Education disruption creates immediate and long-term child protection and learning-continuity concerns.
futureCapacityNeed: Temporary learning must transition into durable education recovery, teacher support, psychosocial support, safeguarding, and youth leadership pathways.
whyItMatters: Prolonged education disruption can affect child development, livelihoods, civic participation, and future social cohesion.
assumptions: Education actors can work through safeguarding protocols.
caveats: Future capacity hypothesis; local validation required.

currentCondition: Water, sanitation, displacement, and health constraints can increase disease-prevention concerns.
futureCapacityNeed: Disease-prevention awareness, WASH coordination, safe-water communication, and referral awareness.
whyItMatters: Water and sanitation disruptions can increase public-health risk.
assumptions: WASH and health actors can coordinate messaging.
caveats: Public-health learning is not medical advice.

currentCondition: Recovery will likely interact with digital tools, remote learning, translation, source verification, and data systems.
futureCapacityNeed: Digital literacy, responsible AI use, data protection, translation tools, remote learning, and safe civic technology.
whyItMatters: Technology can help or harm depending on design, privacy, access, and accountability.
assumptions: Digital infrastructure is available in some form.

currentCondition: Long-term recovery involves trauma, identity, narrative, trust, youth agency, and institutional repair.
futureCapacityNeed: Long-term social repair, intergroup understanding, trauma-informed dialogue, narrative work, youth leadership, and practical peacebuilding infrastructure.
whyItMatters: Generational recovery requires civic trust, dignity, wellbeing, and capacity for coexistence.
assumptions: Conditions eventually allow sustained civic and peacebuilding work.
Programs are partner-mediated and locally validated.

currentCondition: Health and WASH disruptions can affect infection prevention and resilient care systems.
futureCapacityNeed: Infection prevention, antibiotic stewardship awareness, public-health surveillance, clean water, sanitation, and health-system capacity.
whyItMatters: Global bacterial infection and antimicrobial resistance risks show why infection prevention and resilient health systems matter.
assumptions: Local data is reviewed before any Gaza-specific claim.
caveats: Global health signal, not a Gaza-specific claim unless locally sourced.

currentCondition: Emergency support may need to connect to early recovery without assuming transition is guaranteed.
futureCapacityNeed: Transition from emergency response to early recovery, including education continuity, health workforce support, housing pathways, youth services, and local civil-society capacity.
whyItMatters: The first year shapes whether emergency systems become recovery systems.
assumptions: Access and governance allow limited transition planning.
caveats: Do not treat transition scenarios as guaranteed.

currentCondition: Young people will carry major recovery, learning, livelihood, and civic burdens.
futureCapacityNeed: Youth leadership pathways, social cohesion skills, conflict transformation, civic participation, digital literacy, and livelihood pathways.
whyItMatters: Young people need agency, skills, dignity, and future orientation as recovery unfolds.
assumptions: Local youth priorities are heard directly through partners.
risks: Treating youth only as a risk category
caveats: Youth pathways involving minors require safeguarding and partner mediation.

currentCondition: Supporters face many claims, organizations, and urgent appeals in a fragmented information space.
futureCapacityNeed: Donors, students, and institutions need better capacity to verify sources, assess organization evidence, and route support responsibly.
whyItMatters: Misdirected support can create harm, confusion, or diversion risk.
assumptions: Public evidence is available for review.
Routing remains through official channels only.
caveats: Evidence language does not certify or endorse organizations.

currentCondition: Future crises may require distributed, locally grounded, technologically aware response capacity.
futureCapacityNeed: Networked humanitarian response, adaptive coordination, crisis communication, local leadership, digital tools, and anticipatory action.
whyItMatters: Recovery systems should strengthen future readiness, not only immediate response.
caveats: Capacity hypothesis; human review and local validation required.
